לְהוֹדִיעַ לְדוֹרוֹת שֶׁהַשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה יְסוֹדוֹת הָעִקָּרִיִּים בְּהַשְׁאָרַת אַדְמוֹ"ר זַצַ"ל כְּפִי הַמּוּבָן בָּזֶה מִדִּבְרֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת
זַ"ל:
א) אֲסֵפָתֵנוּ עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁבָּזֶה מִמֵּילָא כָּלוּל גַּם
 אֲמִירַת הָעֲשָׂרָה קַפִּיטְל תְּהִלִּים עַל צִיוּנוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
 ב) עֵסֶק הַהַדְפָּסָה:
 ג) וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר תָּמִיד עַל צִיוּנוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
וְהִנֵּה בְּעִנְיַן הָרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּבָר כָּתַבְתִּי מִזֶּה קְצָת בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. וּבְעִנְיַן הַהַדְפָּסָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָאֵר אֲפִלּוּ בְּעַל פֶּה. וּבְעִנְיַן הַנֵּר תָּמִיד עַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר הַמִּדּוֹת מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב שָׁם אַדְמוֹ"ר זַ"ל שֶׁבִּזְכוּת הַנֵּר תָּמִיד שֶׁמַּדְלִיקִין מִשֶּׁמֶן זַיִת נִצּוֹלִין מִגְּזֵרוֹת שְׁמָד. וּמִמֵּילָא מוּבָן מִזֶּה בְּאַלְפֵי אֲלָפִים קַל וָחֹמֶר לְהַנֵּר תָּמִיד שֶׁאֵצֶל קִבְרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ, כְּפִי הַמּוּבָא מִזֶּה בְּקֻנְטְרֵס הַנִּקְרָא "חָכְמָה וּבִינָה" עַיֵּן שָׁם וְתָבִין מִזֶּה לְמַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בְּלִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן בְּעִנְיַן קִבְרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ שֶׁעוֹסֵק בָּזֶה לְהַעֲלוֹת מִשְּׁמָד לְרָצוֹן. וּבְלִקּוּטֵי הֲלָכוֹת הִלְכוֹת בִּרְכַּת הַשַּׁחַר הֲלָכָה ה' מְבֹאָר מִשָּׁם שֶׁגַּם כָּל הַתַּאֲווֹת וְהַמִּדּוֹת רָעוֹת בִּפְרָט הָאֶפִּיקוֹרְסוּת הַכֹּל כָּלוּל בְּעִנְיַן שְׁמָד הַנַּ"ל. וּמִצֵּרוּף כָּל הָעִנְיָנִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּיַחַד הִפְלִיג מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל בִּדְבַר הַנֵּר תָּמִיד עַד אֵין שִׁעוּר וָעֵרֶךְ, כֵּן שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּפֵרוּשׁ
מֵאָבִי זַ"ל:
וְזֶה יָדוּעַ שֶׁסְּגֻלַּת כָּל מִצְוָה וְהַנְהָגָה שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת הִיא דַּוְקָא כְּפִי הַפְּרָטִים שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ מִזֶּה בְּכָל דָּבָר. כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁבְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתֵּצֵא אֶל הַפֹּעַל מֵהַרְכָּבַת הַסַּמִּים כֹּחַ הָרְפוּאָה לְהַמַּחֲלָה כִּי־אִם אִם עָשׂוּ מְכֻוָּן מַמָּשׁ בְּכָל הַפְּרָטִים שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִפִּי הָרוֹפֵא (אִם הָיָה בְּנִמְצָא הָרוֹפֵא הָאֲמִתִּי), כְּמוֹ כֵן מַמָּשׁ בָּחֳלִי הַנֶּפֶשׁ, לְמָשָׁל בְּעִנְיַן הָעֲשָׂרָה קַפִּיטְל תְּהִלִּים שֶׁהֵם מְסֻגָּלִים לִפְגַם הַבְּרִית רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן, וְכֵן בְּעִנְיַן
הַנֵּר תָּמִיד שֶׁדִּקְדֵּק אַדְמוֹ"ר זַצַ"ל וּפָּרַט בִּפְרָט שֶׁמֶן זַיִת:
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַדְמוֹ"ר זַצַ"ל שֶׁכָּל תִּינוֹק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ קֹדֶם שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים יִהְיֶה שָׁמוּר מִן הַחֵטְא עַד יוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ, כִּמְדֻמֶּה לִי שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר זֹאת רַק לְעִנְיַן מִקְרֵה לַיְלָה, וְכֵן מוּבָן מֵהַזְּמַן שֶׁתָּפַס לָזֶה וְכוּ'. וְגַם נִרְאֶה לַעֲנִיּוּת דַּעְתִּי שֶׁהָיְתָה כַּוָּנָתוֹ גַּם אַחַר הִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ לְכָל תִּינוֹק שֶׁיָּבֹא אֶצְלוֹ קֹדֶם שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים וִיקַיֵּם כְּמַאֲמָרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בִּנְתִינַת הַצְּדָקָה וַאֲמִירַת הַיּוּ"ד
קַאפִּיטְל תְּהִלִּים, (וְיָדַעְתִּי מֵאֶחָד שֶׁבָּחַן זֹאת וְכֵן הֲוָה):
עַל אוֹדוֹת תּוֹעֶלֶת הַתְּפִלָּה (וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן הַתּוֹעֶלֶת שֶׁל הַצְּדָקָה וּשְׁאָר עֵצוֹת שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת) דְּזִימְנִין דְּלָא שָׁמַע, וְגַם בְּזִימְנִין דְּשָׁמַע נִמְצָא שִׁנּוּיִים רַבִּים, כִּי לִפְעָמִים נִתְקַבְּלָה הַתְּפִלָּה בַּפַּעַם הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְלִפְעָמִים מֻכְרָח לְהַרְבּוֹת בָּהּ. מוּבָן לְפִי עֲנִיּוּת דַּעְתִּי מִדִּבְרֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה בְּאַרְבָּעִים יוֹם רְצוּפִים בְּלִי דִּלּוּג בֵּינְתַיִם מְסֻגֶּלֶת בְּיוֹתֵר
לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַבַּקָּשָׁה אֶל הַפֹּעַל:
segments.en:
מה Reb Hillel the Shochet — "If You Had Waited a Little Longer, You Would Have Come to Me in Your Socks" — and the Fulfilled Prophecy

In one city there was a shochet u'vodek [ritual slaughterer and inspector] named Reb Hillel. And he was close to Admoyr z"tl — but afterwards distanced himself and did not travel to him for several years. Afterwards he returned and came to him — but was afraid to appear before him, and asked a man of his close disciples to accompany him to Admoyr z"tl. And he went with him.

And Admoyr z"tl was at that time in his study-hall. And when they came to the entrance and opened it, a great fear and awe fell upon them — and the man mentioned above remained standing behind the door, while Reb Hillel entered the study-hall. And he remained standing near the door. And our master z"l, when he saw a person standing near the door, approached him and greeted him — and said in these words:

"S'iz du Hillel! Du zolst geveyzn vartn noch a bisel — volstu geveyzn gekumen tzu mir mit di zokin."

("It is you, Hillel! Had you waited a little while longer — you would have come to me in your socks" — that is, after his death.)

And Reb Hillel began to weep greatly before him — for great fear fell upon him upon hearing these words from the mouth of Admoyr z"tl. And afterwards our master z"l rebuked him for having distanced himself from him for such a long time without traveling to him, and said: "Now I tell you that you must uproot your residence to another city. And if you do not obey me — you will surely regret it."

And afterwards Reb Hillel traveled away from him — and was not willing to return to his home, but only traveled to a certain nearby city and sent a letter to his wife that he would sell his chazakah [tenure] on the slaughtering rights and she should sell the house — for he was compelled to uproot his residence from there. And so it was — he sold the slaughtering rights and she sold the house. But afterwards a controversy arose from one neighbor who claimed that he held right of pre-emption [ bar mitzra ] on his house — to finalize the sale of the house — and [Reb Hillel] would not remain there at all, only once the matter was settled he would travel away. And he agreed to this — for he thought that such a small thing would not harm him, since he would not remain there at all. And he traveled there — and immediately died in that very city. And the words of Admoyr z"l were fulfilled.

מו The Breslov Magnate's Son — the Baal Shem Tov in the Garden at Night; "I Accomplished for You — but Not for Myself"; the Couple Who Finally Divorced and Had Children

In Breslov there was a wealthy man who was close to Admoyr z"tl — and he had an only son, and made a match for him with the granddaughter of the Baal Shem Tov z"tl. And when the time of the wedding arrived — at that same time a child passed away from our master z"l. And our master z"l observed the seven days of mourning [ shiva ] outside the city — for he had rented lodgings there that had a garden before them — since he was not in good health. And he took with him Reb Chayyim Sarahs to serve him there.

Now the wealthy man mentioned above, before traveling to his son's chupa , went with him [the son] to Admoyr z"tl to take leave of him — and they received leave from him and traveled on their way. In that night our master z"l awoke from his sleep, washed his hands, and said to Reb Chayyim: "Come with me." And he went with him to the garden — and our master z"l ran there among the trees back and forth. And Reb Chayyim was very frightened when he saw this — until the hairs of his head stood on end.

Meanwhile our master z"l came to him and said: "Did you see? For the Baal Shem Tov — the grandfather of the bride — came to me and said that he does not want the groom and wishes to take him. And the bride is an orphan." Upon hearing this, Reb Chayyim became even more frightened — and he stood there while his knees knocked one against the other.

And immediately Admoyr z"tl came again to him and said: "I have accomplished [before the Baal Shem Tov] that he should not take the groom — only that there will be no children for them. And afterwards they went inside.

And behold — the next day at noon, Reb Chayyim was standing outside and saw a special messenger from the mechutunim [the wedding party] running to Admoyr z"tl, reporting that the groom had become ill on the road and it was impossible in any way to travel with him to the wedding — and he begged him to arouse mercy on his behalf. And our master z"l said to him: "Return on your way — the groom will be well and they should travel with him to the wedding and erect the chupa ." And immediately the messenger returned on his way. And Reb Chayyim marveled greatly — for he knew what had occurred the previous night. And the wedding took place then. But the words of Admoyr z"tl were fulfilled — that there would be no children for them. And they lived together, that couple, and had no children.

And after several years following the passing of Admoyr z"tl, the Rav Reb Tzvi Aryeh, Moreh Tzedek of Breslov — who was the son-in-law of Reb Chayyim Sarahs mentioned above — endeavored that they should divorce, because his father-in-law Reb Chayyim had told him the entire story above. And the Rav Reb Tzvi Aryeh himself arranged the bill of divorce for them — and afterwards they both had children. This story was recounted by the Rav Reb Tzvi Aryeh z"l himself. [And see above in section 43.]

מז At Aleksandrivke — The Rebbe Studies Mishnah, the Father-in-Law Faints, and the Name of Admoyr Becomes Known as a Tzadik of the Generation

At the time when Admoyr z"tl was still at the table of his father-in-law Reb Efraim z"l in the village of Husyatin — and [Reb Efraim's] yahrtzeit [anniversary of his father's death] arrived and he traveled to Aleksandrivke nearby, taking Admoyr z"tl with him. And when they came to the study-hall and the young men there, upon seeing Admoyr z"tl for the first time, were very pleased to enter into conversation with him — but did not know how to begin.

After the prayer, Reb Efraim z"l gave them old wine as is customary — and the young men asked Reb Efraim mentioned above to instruct his son-in-law — that is, Admoyr z"tl — to study a chapter of Mishnah. And so he did. And [the Rebbe] turned himself to face the eastern wall, took a Mishnah, placed it on the stand, and studied — and lingered in his study so long that it became embarrassing. And the young men waited for him to complete his study, so that they could drink the whisky and through this drink a toast [ lchayyim ] to Admoyr z"tl as well — and thereby they would have a connection to enter into conversation with him.

And when they saw that he was lingering very long in his study, they asked the Rav Reb Efraim to tell him to finish the study. And Admoyr extended his hand toward the face of his father-in-law — and [the father-in-law] fainted. And they began to revive him. And when he came around, they asked him what had happened. And he answered them: when Admoyr z"tl extended his hand toward his face, he saw the departed one — the one whose yahrtzeit was being observed — standing before him and saying: "To a son-in-law such as this one bids to study Mishnah?!" And he was frightened and fainted.

They saw [this] and were very greatly astonished. And from then onward the name of Admoyr z"tl became known — that he was among the Tzadikim of the generation. And several people began to travel to him — and drew close through him to the service of Hashem, may He be blessed.

The Three Pillars — The Heritage Left by Admoyr z"tl for the Generations שְׁלֹשָׁה יְסוֹדוֹת הָעִקָּרִיִּים בְּהַשְׁאָרַת אַדְמוֹ"ר זַצַ"ל

To make known to future generations the three fundamental pillars that are the essential legacy left behind by Admoyr z"tl — as understood from this from the words of Moharan"as z"l:

The Three Pillars of the Legacy of Admoyr z"tl Our gathering on Rosh HaShonoh — in which is also inherently included the recitation of the Ten Chapters of Psalms [Asarah Kapitlach Tehillim] at his holy gravestone [tziyun]. The occupation with printing [of his books]. The continual kindling of the lamp [ner tamid] at his holy gravestone.

Now regarding the matter of Rosh HaShonoh — I have already written somewhat of this in another place. And regarding the matter of printing — it is impossible to explain even orally. And regarding the matter of the ner tamid — see in Sefer HaMidos what Admoyr z"l wrote there: that through the merit of the ner tamid kindled from olive oil, one is saved from decrees of religious persecution [ shemad ]. And from this, the kal va'chomer [inference from minor to major] for the ner tamid at his holy grave is understood by thousands upon thousands of logical steps — as is brought from this in the booklet called "Chochmo uVino" — see there. And you will understand from this what is brought in Likutay Moharan regarding the grave of Moshe and his passing — which deals with this: to elevate from apostasy [ shemad ] to acceptance [ ratzon ]. And in Likutay Halachos , Laws of the Morning Blessings, Halacho 5 — it is explained therefrom that also all the desires and evil character-traits, and in particular heresy [ epikorsus ], are all included in the matter of shemad mentioned above. And from the combination of all these matters together, Moharan"as z"l spoke of the matter of the ner tamid without measure and reckoning. So I heard explicitly from my father z"l.

And it is known that the virtue of every mitzva and practice of the truly righteous is specifically according to the particulars in which they were commanded regarding every matter — for just as in physical matters it is impossible for the healing power to be actualized from the compounding of the medicines for the ailment, except if they were done in exact correspondence to all the particulars as they came forth from the mouth of the physician [if a true physician were to exist] — so too precisely in the ailment of the soul. For example: regarding the Ten Chapters of Psalms which are a segulah [spiritual remedy] for the blemishing of the covenant [ plag ha'bris ], G-d protect us; and likewise regarding the ner tamid — wherein Admoyr z"tl was meticulous and specified in particular: olive oil.

What Admoyr z"tl said — that every child who comes before him [to his tziyun ] before the age of seven will be guarded from sin until the day of his wedding. It seems to me that he said this only regarding the matter of seminal emission [ mikre layla ] — and so it is understood from the time-frame he applied to it, etc. And it also appears to me in my humble understanding that his intention was also after his passing — for every child who will come before him before the age of seven and will fulfill according to his holy saying — with the giving of tzedakah and the recitation of the Ten Chapters of Psalms. [And I know of one who tested this — and so it was.]

Regarding the benefit of prayer — and likewise the benefit of tzedakah and the other counsels of the truly righteous — that sometimes [the prayer] is not heard; and even when it is heard, many variations are found. For sometimes the prayer was accepted at the first time, and sometimes one is compelled to multiply it. I understand, in my humble view, from the words of Moharan"as z"l that I heard orally: that prayer [at his tziyun ] for forty consecutive days without skipping any in between is an especially efficacious segulah for bringing the request to actualization.
